skills.name: stampede-setup
skills.description: Use in a stampede Grok Bot's first conversation, or whenever the user asks to set up, connect, repair or test stampede: guides setup of the bot's computer and the user's Mac (Tailscale, SSH key, Herdr, stampede, event webhook), runs an end-to-end test job, then offers routines and rolling stampede out to the user's other bots.
skills.content:
---
name: stampede-setup
description: >-
  Use in a stampede Grok Bot's first conversation, or whenever the user asks to
  set up, connect, repair or test stampede: guides setup of the bot's computer
  and the user's Mac (Tailscale, SSH key, Herdr, stampede, event webhook), runs
  an end-to-end test job, then offers routines and rolling stampede out to the
  user's other bots.
---
# stampede setup

Gets stampede (https://github.com/vib-z/stampede) working between your Grok Bot and your Mac, end to end, in one conversation. Herdr and the agents run on your Mac; the bot reaches it over SSH on Tailscale and hears back through a webhook, so it never polls.

Source of truth, read from a fresh clone on the bot's computer before each step and follow it where it differs from this recipe: `README.md`, `docs/SETUP.md`, `remote/grokbot/` (README, tailscale, ssh, herdr, webhook, send, in that order), `remote/events.md`, `remote/watchdogs.md`, `skills/grokbot-herdr/SKILL.md` and `skills/herdr-fleet/SKILL.md`.

## Rules for the whole flow
- Talk to the user as "you". Short steps, one at a time. No em or en dashes.
- Ask before anything risky on the user's Mac: installing software, changing settings, writing config, trusting a folder. Read-only checks need no ask.
- Never ask for a password, key, token or webhook secret in chat. Use a secret-request or the vault, and never print one back.
- Never start or stop the Herdr server or its screen. Never run `tailscale down` over SSH. Never run bare `herdr` over SSH (it opens the screen and hangs).
- Every agent run, even a tiny one, happens inside Herdr in a pane of the bot's own tagged workspace and is prompted with `herdr-send`. Never bare `claude -p` or `codex` over SSH.
- Updates only via `stampede update` (or `herdr plugin update stampede` for a Herdr-managed install), never a manual `git pull`.
- Never close a workspace or pane without the user's yes.
- Skip any step that is already done; prove it with a check instead of asking.

## 1. Ask first
Ask these together, in plain text:
- Is stampede already installed on your Mac? (If unsure, offer to check over SSH once connected: `stampede --version`.)
- Which coding agents do you use: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes? (Claude Code is the lead; the others are optional workers.)
- What should I call you?
- A short lowercase slug for this bot, for its Herdr owner tag (default: the bot's name, lowercased).
Save the answers to memory.

## 2. The bot's computer
1. Tailscale: run the `tailscale-setup` skill to put the bot's computer on the user's tailnet. Verify with `tailscale status`.
2. Clone stampede for reference and skills: `git clone https://github.com/vib-z/stampede.git ~/stampede` (or `stampede update` in an existing clone). Make sure the `grokbot-herdr` and `herdr-fleet` skills are available to this bot; if they are not in the skill catalog, save them from the clone's `skills/` folder with UpdateSkill, unchanged.
3. SSH key: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/stampede_mac -N ''` if missing. Show only the PUBLIC key (`.pub`) for the user to add on the Mac.
Nothing about Herdr runs on the bot's computer.

## 3. The user's Mac (only what is missing)
If stampede is already installed, skip to the checks in step 4. Otherwise guide the user, one step at a time, waiting for them to say done:
1. Tailscale on the Mac, same tailnet, and keep the Mac awake while jobs run (System Settings, Energy).
2. Remote Login on (System Settings, General, Sharing) and the bot's public key appended to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`.
3. Herdr from https://herdr.dev/docs/, then start the Herdr server themselves.
4. Each agent CLI they use, started once by hand to sign in.
5. stampede: `git clone https://github.com/vib-z/stampede.git ~/stampede && cd ~/stampede && ./install.sh --dry-run && ./install.sh`, or `herdr plugin install vib-z/stampede`. This links herdr-fleet, grokbot-herdr and share-plan into the agents' skills and puts `stampede`, `fleet-job` and the `herdr-*` helpers in `~/.local/bin`. `~/.local/bin` must be on PATH, also for non-interactive SSH.
6. The unattended steps from docs/SETUP.md: `herdr-trust <repo dir>` per repo and the Claude auto-mode settings.
Once SSH works (step 4), you may run install commands yourself over SSH after a yes.

## 4. Connect and check
1. Add an SSH alias on the bot's computer (`~/.ssh/config`, HostName from `tailscale status`). Call it `mac` unless the user prefers another.
2. `tailscale ping <machine>`, then `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 mac 'export PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; herdr --version; stampede --version'`.
3. Webhook: create a routine on this bot with a webhook trigger (read the `routines` skill) whose prompt says: a Herdr event arrived; read that pane once, report to the user in plain words, ask the user on a `question` or `gate` event, and never approve a gate without their yes. Get its URL and secret into the Mac's route file `~/.config/herdr-events/routes/<slug>` (chmod 600) without the secret passing through chat: write it over SSH from a secret-request env var, or have the user paste it there themselves.
4. Relay pieces from remote/events.md and remote/watchdogs.md: the Herdr plugin event hook, the Claude and Codex hooks, the watchdog and queue flusher. Ask before installing each.
5. `ssh mac 'herdr-doctor --relay'`. Exit 0 goes on. Exit 1: report the PROBLEM lines in plain words, fix what is yours to fix, repeat.
6. `herdr-event-post source=test state=done pane=test` with `HERDR_EVENTS_OWNER=<slug>` and confirm the routine woke.

## 5. End-to-end test
Follow grokbot-herdr steps 1 to 4 for a small job: create `bot-stampede-test` workspace with `--no-focus` in a scratch folder under the trust root, tag it with `herdr-events-owner <ws> <slug>`, start one Claude agent in the root pane, read the screen once, and `herdr-send` it: "Create hello.txt containing 'stampede works', then stop." End the turn. When the done event arrives, read the pane once, confirm the file exists, and tell the user it worked. Ask whether to close the test workspace; close only on yes.

## 6. Routines
Ask what coding or maintenance tasks they repeat (dependency bumps, test runs, PR reviews, release notes). Offer two or three routines that each run as a sized stampede job on the Mac; create the ones they pick. Each routine prompt says to size the job first and never poll.

## 7. Roll out to other bots
Ask once: do you want all your Grok Bots to use stampede for coding and agent work? If yes, for each bot they name: share the `grokbot-herdr` skill (skills are shared across bots already; tell that bot about it), give it its own slug and route file on the Mac pointing at its own webhook routine, and SendToAgent it a short brief: run Herdr work through grokbot-herdr, tag workspaces with its slug, never poll, ask before closing. If no, leave it.

## Done
Tell the user in two or three sentences what is connected, the test result, and which routines exist. Remind them updates come with `stampede update`.

skills.name: grokbot-herdr
skills.description: FIRST skill to read whenever a Grok Bot needs Herdr on the owner's Mac: handles the remote entry from the box (SSH over Tailscale, health check, workspace lookup, safe agent start), then hands off to herdr, herdr-fleet and moshi-best-practices for the actual work.
skills.content:
---
name: grokbot-herdr
description: >-
  FIRST skill to read whenever a Grok Bot needs Herdr on the owner's Mac:
  handles the remote entry from the box (SSH over Tailscale, health check,
  workspace lookup, safe agent start), then hands off to herdr, herdr-fleet and
  moshi-best-practices for the actual work.
---
> **STRICT, every bot:** tag the Herdr workspace with your bot slug before agents start, launch and exit, never poll or wait on a job (no `herdr agent wait` for its result, sleep loops, repeated reads or watcher executors). Act only when the relayed event arrives. Bounded startup checks are fine: `agent start`, `herdr-send` and `agent wait <name> --until idle --timeout 30000` after clearing a startup dialog.
# grokbot-herdr: remote entry to Herdr on the owner's Mac

## First look here
You are a Grok Bot on the box, OUTSIDE Herdr. Before any Herdr work:
1. Read this skill and do steps 1-4 below (connect, health check, workspace, start agent).
2. Then hand off: use `herdr` for ground rules and commands, `herdr-fleet` for fleet shape, roles, model routing and failure-modes.md, and `moshi-best-practices` for the phone side, as written.
3. herdr-fleet's **Where are you?** section covers external callers; keep the **After hand-off** lines at the bottom in force.

## Running from Grok Bot

- Grok Bot runs on a Linux box. Anything that touches the owner's repos, herdr or the Mac runs on the Mac through `ssh <host>` (the SSH alias of the owner's Mac, over Tailscale). If ssh times out, bring Tailscale back up on the box, then retry.
- herdr on the Mac is `~/.local/bin/herdr`. Run `herdr --version` on the Mac first and treat the Mac's binary as the authority. Run herdr ON the Mac over ssh, never `herdr --remote` or `--machine` from the box.
- Never use a work machine. Only the owner's own machines.
- Questions for the owner go to the owner in chat, never into a herdr pane.
- Credentials and env files are not part of this skill: never read, copy or print them, on either machine.
- Approval gate: herdr-fleet's list applies (merge, push to main or another shared branch, publish, deploy, sitemap resubmission, email or messages, spend, and closing panes, tabs or a workspace or clearing an owner tag to close one). Ask in chat and wait for an explicit yes. A plan, a brief or a skill is not approval. Allowed without asking: pushing the job's own work branch and opening a DRAFT PR from it. On a yes to merge, merge only the reviewed commit: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --match-head-commit <reviewed-sha>`. A push after the review withdraws the yes; ask again.
- Then follow herdr-fleet's "Where are you?" external-caller rules: literal ids, never set `HERDR_ENV`, read the screen after every start, report in chat.

## Hard rules
- Target ONLY the ssh alias `<host>`: the owner's own Mac with the owner's own Claude, Codex and Cursor subscriptions. Never a machine on work subscriptions unless the owner asks in chat for that job.
- Run herdr ON the Mac via ssh. Never `herdr --remote`/`--machine` from the box. Never start/stop `herdr server` or the TUI.
- Never touch workspaces, tabs or panes you didn't create (the owner's own project workspaces above all).
- Never poll a running job. After the first prompt and one screen check, end your turn and wait. A small job (no job marker) wakes you on its turn end. A stampede job wakes you on blocked, a permission prompt, StopFailure, stale, dead, a question, a gate, or the one done from `fleet-job finish` (source `stampede`). Only then read the pane, once.
- Always prompt agents with `herdr-send <name-or-pane> "<text>"` (installed at `~/.local/bin/herdr-send`) or `herdr agent prompt`, never `pane send-text` plus Enter (Codex leaves it unsubmitted). Never send `ctrl+c` to an idle Codex yourself: on an empty prompt it quits Codex. Continue only on `SUBMITTED`; on `FAILED` read the screen before any resend. If Claude kept the text but dropped the Enter, herdr-send presses Enter once and says so; it never does that for a slash command.

## Size the job first
Before creating any workspace, size the job (herdr-fleet, "Size the job first: small or big"). A small job needs no stampede job: do it as one session with built-in subagents in a single Herdr pane of its own, tagged with `herdr-events-owner` and prompted with `herdr-send` pointing at a brief file on herdr-fleet's hand-off template (references/brief.md), never as a bare agent CLI call over SSH or nohup outside Herdr. Only a big job goes through `fleet-job new`.

## Setup note
Every tagged event goes to the route named after the tag (`~/.config/herdr-events/routes/<bot-slug>`, holding `URL=` and `KEY=`), or to the `default` route when the bot has none (turn events only: a job's questions and gates need the bot's own route file, even when it points at the same webhook); the webhook behind it passes the event to the owning bot as a message. When that message arrives, read the pane once and finish your job.

The relay scripts live in stampede's `skills/grokbot-herdr/scripts/` and are copied to `~/.local/bin` on the Mac (back up the live copy first). `herdr-reopen-snapshot` is copied the same way. What reaches your bot:
- While `~/.config/herdr-events/jobs/<workspace>` exists (`fleet-job new` writes it, `fleet-job finish` removes it), plain turn ends in that workspace stay on the machine. Still sent: `blocked` and permission prompts (one per pane per 120 s), `StopFailure`, `stale`, `dead`, questions, gates, and that one finish. With no marker, turn ends for one pane within 15 s are one event, and `idle_prompt` 60 s after a turn end is dropped. A Codex turn with no Herdr pane is never sent.
- Codex sub-agents, the `--approve-for-me` guardian and Codex's chat-title side conversation never report "done"; only the agent's own turn does.
- After an outage only each pane's newest queued event is delivered; older ones go to `~/.herdr-events/dead/*.superseded`.
- Owner tags for workspaces gone a day, and malformed tags, are removed by the watchdog.

## Step 1. Connect
Every call: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 <host> '<herdr command>'`. If herdr isn't found, prefix `export PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH;`.

## Step 2. Health check
`ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 <host> '~/.local/bin/herdr-doctor --relay'` (read only; one `ok`, `warn` or `PROBLEM` line per check, exit 1 on a PROBLEM).
- Exit 0: go on. Mention any `warn` line in your report; never fix it yourself unless it is yours.
- Exit 1: stop and tell the owner the PROBLEM lines (a broken relay means your job's events would never reach you).
- ssh fails: bring Tailscale back up on the box, then retry once. Still failing: stop and tell the owner (usually the Mac is asleep or offline).
- herdr server not running or erroring: stop and tell the owner; don't start it.

## Step 3. Workspace (by name, never env vars)
- Existing project workspace id: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <host> 'herdr workspace list' | jq -r '.result.workspaces[]|select(.label=="<project>").workspace_id'`
- Bot work: create your own: `herdr workspace create --cwd <repo dir> --label bot-<task> --no-focus`. Record the returned literal ids (`.result.workspace.workspace_id`, `.result.tab.tab_id`, `.result.root_pane.pane_id`). **First tab rule:** `workspace create` already makes tab 1 with a root pane. Never leave it empty: use it for the first workstream (`herdr tab rename`, and put the lead or first agent in the root pane), and only `tab create` for further workstreams. When the owner says yes to closing and you created the workspace, close the whole workspace (`herdr workspace close <ws>`).
- Tag the owner right away: `~/.local/bin/herdr-events-owner <wK> <your-bot-slug>`. `<wK>` is the literal workspace id, never the object; the script refuses anything that is not a live workspace id. For one-off commands in a pane, also set `HERDR_EVENTS_OWNER=<your-bot-slug>`. Untagged workspaces are only logged, never sent.

## Step 4. Start an agent safely
Write the owner's words to `ask.md` on the box and copy it to the Mac (`ssh -o BatchMode=yes <host> 'cat > /tmp/ask-<task>.md' < ask.md`), then run `fleet-job new --file /tmp/ask-<task>.md --pane <wK root pane>` there, after the owner tag; in an existing project workspace use `--workspace wK` instead. It makes the job folder `<repo>/.herdr-<slug>/`, starts the lead `lead-<slug>` on Claude with its hooks, and prints the lead's name and the job folder; tell the owner the lead's name. When the owner asked to see the plan first, add `--review` and use the share-plan skill.
- `agent_not_ready` = blocked at a dialog. Some dialogs report `idle` instead, so after every start read the screen once: `herdr agent read <name> --source visible --lines 30`.
- Codex "Update available": the default is "Update now", which runs npm. Press `herdr agent send-keys <name> esc` to skip it; never Enter.
- Claude "New MCP server found in this project": `herdr agent send-keys <name> enter` on the default, "Continue without using this MCP server".
- Folder trust: before starting agents in a repo under the trust root (`FLEET_TRUST_ROOT`, default `~/code`), run `~/.local/bin/herdr-trust <repo dir>`. If a trust dialog still shows, Claude: `send-keys down`, read to confirm "Yes, I trust this folder" is selected, then `send-keys enter` as a separate call; Codex: `send-keys enter` on "Trust and continue".
- After clearing a dialog: `herdr agent wait <name> --until idle --timeout 30000`, then read the screen once more before the first prompt.
- Login, payment, account switch, trust for a folder outside the trust root, or anything unfamiliar: stop and ask the owner.
- Reopen record: `fleet-job new` records the lead's start in `<job dir>/agents.tsv`; `herdr-reopen-snapshot wK <job dir>` writes `REOPEN.md` and `reopen.sh`. Refresh it after every later start and before any close.

Then end your turn. On an event, read the new lines of `<job dir>/inbox.log` once. A `QUESTION` line or a `question` event for the owner: ask in chat, then `fleet-job tell <job dir> lead "<their words>"`. A gate comes back as a `gate` event (job, gate, exact action, PR, commit): ask the owner in chat with those, and only on their yes run `fleet-job approve-gate <job dir> <gate> --sha <commit> --by "owner in <bot> chat"`; on a no or anything else, `fleet-job tell` the lead their words. Never type a yes into a pane, approve a gate the owner did not answer, or change its commit; a push after the yes withdraws it.

## After hand-off
herdr-fleet now handles external callers; follow its **Where are you?** section. Also keep:
- The ask you write for `fleet-job new` names every parallel step as a pane (`research-web` in tab `research`, `review-claude`), or the lead runs it as a hidden built-in subagent. The lead is woken by hooks, so do not add rules about waiting.
- Moshi: read-only from bots; if the box's pairing is dead, report, never re-pair.
- Done: never close anything, or clear the owner tag, by yourself when the job ends. Refresh the reopen record, leave the workspace open, and end your report with: "Close workspace <label>? Reopen with <job dir>/reopen.sh." No answer is a no. Only after the owner's explicit yes: exit the agents gracefully (`/exit`, `/quit` for Codex), `herdr-reopen-snapshot wK <job dir>`, `herdr-events-owner wK --clear`, then `herdr workspace close wK`, only for workspaces you created. Never close project workspaces.

## Official docs
- https://herdr.dev/docs/cli-reference/
- https://herdr.dev/docs/agent-automation/

Re-check both, and `herdr <cmd> --help` on the Mac, after Herdr is upgraded or when a command fails. Where they differ the installed binary wins.

skills.name: herdr-fleet
skills.description: Playbook for running a multi-agent fleet in Herdr: one workspace per project, a tab per workstream and a pane per agent. A lead writes briefs, starts Claude or Codex agents on models matched to each task, runs review loops and integrates the result. Use for parallel agent work in Herdr, or whenever a brief inside a Herdr pane asks for parallel work.
skills.content:
---
name: herdr-fleet
description: >-
  Playbook for running a multi-agent fleet in Herdr: one workspace per project,
  a tab per workstream and a pane per agent. A lead writes briefs, starts Claude
  or Codex agents on models matched to each task, runs review loops and
  integrates the result. Use for parallel agent work in Herdr, or whenever a
  brief inside a Herdr pane asks for parallel work.
---
# herdr fleet

The built-in skill (`herdr --skill`) is the command reference. This is how to run teams on top of it. The installed binary is the authority: check syntax with `herdr agent`, `herdr pane`, `herdr tab`, `herdr workspace`. Never run bare `herdr` (it attaches the TUI).

> **Strict rule for bots launching jobs from outside Herdr:** tag the workspace with `herdr-events-owner <ws> <bot-slug>` before any agent starts, then launch and exit. Never poll or wait on a job. Stuck events, and one `fleet-job finish` when the job ends, are relayed to the owning bot, which reads the result once. See grokbot-herdr. A lead inside Herdr is woken by hooks instead.

## Where are you?
- **Inside a Herdr pane** (`test "${HERDR_ENV:-}" = 1`): use `$HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, `$HERDR_PANE_ID` and `--current`.
- **External caller** (a bot reaching the Mac over ssh): first run your entry skill (`grokbot-herdr`). Never set `HERDR_ENV`. Replace those variables with literal ids (e.g. `w1`, `w1:p1`). Run herdr ON the Mac over ssh, never `--remote` or `--machine`. Only the owner's own machines. Report in your own chat, not in a lead pane.

Read live state before changing anything: `herdr workspace list`, `herdr tab list --workspace <ws>`, `herdr agent list`.

## Size the job first: small or big
Size on four questions: **length** (under about an hour, or hours or overnight), **agents** (one family, or a mix), **risk** (does anything leave the machine: merge, push, send, spend, publish, deploy) and **durability** (must it survive a restart).
- **Small** (all four small): no stampede job. One agent session with its built-in subagents, still inside Herdr: its own tagged pane, prompted with `herdr-send` pointing at a brief on the hand-off template. Never a bare agent CLI call over SSH.
- **Big** (any one big): a stampede job with gates and a reopen record.
- **Unsure:** start small, promote the moment a big signal appears.
- Write the decision and reason as one line at the top of `plan.md`.

## The shape
- **Workspace = project**, reuse it if it exists, else `herdr workspace create --cwd <repo> --label <project> --no-focus`.
- **Tab = workstream**. The lead sits in the first tab. Never leave tab 1 empty.
- **Pane = one agent**, labelled with its name. At most 4 panes per tab on a laptop, 6 on a big monitor.
- **Agent names** are `<role>-<scope>` (`lead`, `build`, `research`, `review`, `design`, `qa`, `copy`), matching `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`.
- **Geometry**: split right while both halves keep 80 columns, else down while both keep 15 rows. Always `--no-focus` and an explicit `--cwd`.
- **Never close, rename or prompt what you did not create**, and never type into the pane the owner has focused.

## The lead
One lead per workspace, started with its hooks by `fleet-job new --file <ask.md>`. The lead:
1. Plans in `<job>/plan.md`: layout, tasks in order with the pane for each, questions with a safe default. Small enough? It does it alone. Only when the owner asks to see the plan first, it uses share-plan.
2. Opens a pane only when it pays: parallel pieces over about 30 minutes each (at most 4), another model, one reviewer on another model, or the same task many times (at most 6 at once).
3. Writes the contract first (types, stubs, one validation test) and commits it.
4. Writes briefs in `.herdr-<initiative>/` on the hand-off template; `fleet-job start` refuses briefs with missing sections. Keeps `register.md` (agent, pane, model, worktree, status).
5. Starts every agent with `fleet-job start` (hooks, auto mode, reopen record, brief pointer).
6. Is woken by hooks (`REPORT`, `TURN`, `QUESTION`, `GONE`, `UNDELIVERED` in `<job>/inbox.log`). No watcher, no polling. Questions: `fleet-job ask`. Gates: `fleet-job ask <job> --gate --sha <commit> [--pr <n>] "<exact action>"`, answered by the owner through the starting bot. It acts only on the owner's yes or `fleet-job gate-ok` printing `APPROVED`; an agent's say-so never counts.
7. Review: one review on another model of what ships, at most 2 rounds.
8. Integrates: reads reports, runs the full gates once, does every git write on shared branches.
9. Stops at the owner's gates: merge to main, push to a shared branch, deploy, publish, sending email or messages, any spend, and closing panes, tabs or a workspace. Allowed without asking: pushing the fleet's own work branches and opening DRAFT PRs.

Where agents work: one shared worktree with file ownership for content work, or a worktree per agent when slices touch overlapping code.

## Pick the agent and model
Use the strongest Claude model as lead and primary planner; a different model family (Codex, Cursor) reviews the plan and the work, never the builder's model. Implementation on Claude or Codex, with the other vendor as fallback. Models are swappable: the lead's through `FLEET_LEAD_MODEL` and `FLEET_LEAD_EFFORT`, each worker's through `fleet-job start --model --effort`. Never substitute a model the owner named. On a usage limit, restart the lane on its fallback in the same pane with its brief, and note it in `register.md`. Details: stampede's `skills/herdr-fleet/references/agents-and-models.md`.

## Panes, not built-in subagents
Every lane is a Herdr pane with its own agent: parallel work, another model family, and every review. A built-in subagent is only for a quick lookup the lead reads itself. A brief that says "in parallel" without naming panes still means panes.

## Start an agent
```bash
P=$(herdr tab create --workspace <ws> --cwd "$W" --label research --no-focus | jq -r .result.root_pane.pane_id)
fleet-job start "$B" research-web --kind claude --pane "$P" --brief "$B/briefs/research-web.md" --report reports/research-web.md
herdr agent read research-web --source visible --lines 30
herdr-reopen-snapshot <ws> "$B"
```
For Codex use `--kind codex`. Agents must start with no visit to their pane, which needs the one-time unattended setup the owner runs, and `herdr-trust <repo dir>` for repos under `~/code`. The lead clears known startup dialogs (folder trust, Codex "Update available" with esc, Claude "New MCP server found" continue without), then `herdr agent wait <name> --until idle --timeout 30000` and reads the screen before the first prompt. It never answers a permission prompt for an action.

## Reopen record
Every job keeps `REOPEN.md` and `reopen.sh` in its job folder, written by `herdr-reopen-snapshot <ws> <job dir>`: workspace label, owner tag, tabs, panes and each agent's CLI, model, session id, brief and start command. `bash <job dir>/reopen.sh` recreates the workspace and resumes every session. Refresh after every start and before any close.

## Talk, watch, review
- A prompt is one line pointing at a file; substance lives in briefs and reports.
- Before every prompt, `herdr agent get <name>`. After a timeout or ssh drop, read the screen before any resend.
- Always prompt with `herdr-send` or `herdr agent prompt`, never `pane send-text` plus Enter, never `ctrl+c` an idle Codex. Continue only on `SUBMITTED`.
- The report file is the completion signal: `reports/<lane>.md` with `Status: DONE` (or `PASS` / `FINDINGS`) in its first 10 lines.
- Known failures and a worked example: stampede's `skills/herdr-fleet/references/`.

## The owner's phone (Moshi)
Questions, approvals and completions reach the owner's phone through Moshi, tagged with workspace and tab, so name tabs and agents after the task.

## Wrap up
Integrate, run the gates once, push the work branch and open a DRAFT PR, then ask before any merge. Record `Reviewed: <sha>`; on the yes, `gh pr merge <n> --squash --match-head-commit <sha>`. A later push withdraws the yes. When done, `fleet-job finish <job> "<one line>"` once.

**Ask before close.** Never close anything automatically. The last step is a question: "Close workspace <label>? Reopen with <job dir>/reopen.sh". No answer is a no. On a yes: exit agents gracefully, refresh the reopen record, clear the owner tag, then close only what you created. Remove only your worktrees, keep the branches.
